raw_response:
I'll reason through this as the farmer, then give the structured plan.

---

I've been at this since I was twenty years old. Know these fields better than I know anything. Seven and a half mu — small, but it feeds us and gives us a little cash.

Same plan as always, mostly. Five mu in the wheat-maize rotation on the east side, two mu and a bit in cotton over on the west patch where the soil is heavier. My son is in Shijiazhuang doing construction work, sends money back when he can. At home it's me, my wife, and the two grandchildren still in school. For the heavy work — tilling, the cotton picking — I hire the village tractor and sometimes a couple of extra hands because my back gives me trouble in autumn.

**Wheat** — I already put down the base fertilizer last October before planting, one bag of that compound fertilizer per mu, the 50-jin bags. Always done it that way. Old Li next door does the same. Now it's spring and the wheat is jointing, so I need to top-dress with urea soon, about half a bag per mu. Scatter it before it rains if I can. I'll water three times — did the pre-planting soak and the winter water already, just the jointing water left now. Usually get 800 jin per mu, maybe 850 if spring rain is good.

**Maize** — Right after wheat comes off in early June, no time to rest. I buy hybrid seed from the village store, the Zhengdan kind — can't save that seed, everyone knows it. No time to plow deep after wheat, I just break up the surface a little, put some base fertilizer down, and get the seed in. Around late July when the stalks are tasseling I haul the urea out again. Usually only need to pump water once for maize, when it's dry at the flowering stage. Gets about 900 jin per mu most years.

**Cotton** — This is the work that ages you. My wife and I handle the spraying together but the picking in August-September is too much for just us now. I'll hire three days of outside help. Plant late April after the cold is finished, usually set out seedlings rather than direct seed — more work up front but fewer gaps. Two waterings. Spray for bollworm twice, maybe three times if it's bad. Cotton gives me cash when wheat and maize prices are low, so I keep the west plot in it even though my back doesn't thank me. Expect about 480 jin per mu of seed cotton.

Total spending this year — seed, fertilizer, chemicals, pump electricity, hired tractor and pickers — probably around 3,400 yuan. Same as last year.
